question: Is the shallow-soil-moisture association with strong chorus activation carried primarily by reactivation of species already observed in the local route/site history rather than by strong choruses with no prior route record?
population: Physically stable NAAMP matched pairs with valid ERA5 swvl1 and at least one strictly prior eligible run in the same route-season stratum.
memory_partition: Use the fixed prior-only strong-activation memory partition: same-site prior strong, same-site prior weak-only, route-only prior, and no-prior-stratum record.
model: Each response ~ rain_contrast + rain72_amount_difference_z + soil1_gain_difference_z + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + C(State) + C(RunNumber), route-clustered covariance.
primary_rule: Reactivation-hydric support if recurrent soil beta has complete positive 95% CI, recurrent soil beta / total soil beta >0.5, and no-prior soil beta does not have a complete positive 95% CI.
secondary: Report same-site share of total soil beta.
Repeat CI3 recurrent vs no-prior partition.
Replace swvl1 with swvl2 for recurrent response.
minimum_gate: At least 1500 prior-history weather-qualified pairs and 300 routes; total strong_new_score soil beta must be estimable.
interpretation: Support would directly connect hydric state to reactivation of previously observed local acoustic populations/templates rather than to genuinely history-free appearance.
No prior record can reflect historical nondetection, not only genuine novelty.
This does not prove continuous occupancy, individual persistence, pond depth, frog body hydration or causal mediation.
